# Silex — Stop Gambling

An iPhone app that blocks gambling across the phone, runs a 90-day evidence-based quit program, and tracks the money you keep. No accounts, no tracking, no ads. Built by Kyrylo Lozovyi. Weekly $4.99 or annual $49.99 with a 3-day free trial.

## Pages

- [Quit gambling for good. Keep the money.](https://trysilex.com/): Silex blocks gambling across your iPhone, walks you through a 90-day evidence-based quit program, and counts the money you keep. No accounts, no ads, no profile of you.
- [Who builds Silex](https://trysilex.com/about/): Silex is built by one developer, Kyrylo Lozovyi, in Kyiv. No investors, no growth team, nothing that profiles you — and a short list of rules the app will not break.
- [The best gambling blocker apps, compared honestly](https://trysilex.com/best-gambling-blocker-apps/): Gamban, BetBlocker, GamBlock and the rest — what each one covers, what it costs, and which to pick. Prices verified from each vendor's own site, with a disclosure: we make one of these.
- [How to block gambling on Android](https://trysilex.com/block-gambling-apps-android/): Android's built-in Private DNS blocks gambling in every app and browser for free, in about two minutes. Plus Digital Wellbeing, Family Link, and which third-party blockers are worth it.
- [How to block gambling sites and apps on iPhone](https://trysilex.com/block-gambling-sites-iphone/): Every working method for blocking gambling on an iPhone — Screen Time, a system-wide DNS profile, Safari content blockers, bank blocks and self-exclusion — with what each one actually covers and how easily you can undo it.
- [How to make your bank decline gambling payments](https://trysilex.com/block-gambling-transactions-bank/): Bank gambling blocks decline payments to betting operators and take days to lift. Which UK banks offer one, what US cardholders can do instead, and why the cooling-off period is the whole point.
- [Gamban alternatives](https://trysilex.com/gamban-alternatives/): Gamban costs £4.99 a month or £29.99 a year. Here are the free and paid alternatives that cover the same job, what each does better, and when Gamban is still the right answer.
- [Gambling debt: where to start](https://trysilex.com/gambling-debt-help/): How to deal with debt from gambling — stop the bleeding, work out what's actually owed, get free charity debt advice, and avoid the consolidation traps aimed at people in exactly this position.
- [Gambling loss calculator](https://trysilex.com/gambling-loss-calculator/): Put in what you lose in a typical week and see the yearly, 5-year and 10-year total, plus what the same money would have compounded to. Runs in your browser; nothing is stored.
- [What happens when you stop gambling](https://trysilex.com/gambling-recovery-timeline/): Withdrawal, sleep, mood, money and the danger points — what the first 90 days after quitting gambling commonly look like, and which weeks people actually relapse in.
- [I gambled again — what to do now](https://trysilex.com/gambling-relapse/): A slip is not the end of quitting — how you interpret it decides what happens next. The abstinence violation effect, the practical first hour after a lapse, and how to turn it into information.
- [The 9-question gambling self-check (PGSI)](https://trysilex.com/gambling-self-check/): Take the Problem Gambling Severity Index (PGSI) — the same 9-question screener clinicians and helplines use. Runs entirely in your browser, stores nothing, sends nothing.
- [Someone you love is gambling](https://trysilex.com/help-someone-with-gambling-addiction/): Practical steps for partners and families: protect the household money first, why paying the debt backfires, how to have the conversation, and where to get support for yourself.
- [How long do gambling urges last?](https://trysilex.com/how-long-do-gambling-urges-last/): A gambling urge behaves like a wave: it rises, crests and falls, usually inside 20 to 30 minutes, whether or not you bet. What the first weeks feel like, and the urge-surfing technique that uses the pattern.
- [How to stop gambling](https://trysilex.com/how-to-stop-gambling/): A practical, evidence-based plan for quitting gambling: the three barriers to put up first, how to ride out an urge, what the first 90 days look like, and where to get free human help.
- [How to stop sports betting](https://trysilex.com/how-to-stop-sports-betting/): Sports betting is harder to quit than casino gambling because the trigger is the sport itself. What to block, what to do about watching games, and how to handle the group chat.
- [How the program was built, and from what](https://trysilex.com/methodology/): The clinical and academic sources behind Silex's 90-day quit-gambling program: CBT for gambling disorder, the PGSI self-check, relapse-prevention research, and the literature on how gambling products are engineered.
- [Privacy Policy](https://trysilex.com/privacy/): Silex runs no servers of its own, holds no accounts, and cannot read anything you write in the app. The full GDPR and UK GDPR notice, including the few places data does leave your phone.
- [Self-exclusion: the strongest block there is](https://trysilex.com/self-exclusion-guide/): How gambling self-exclusion works in the UK via GAMSTOP and in the US state by state, what it covers, what it misses, and why it is the strongest layer available — free, and irreversible on purpose.
- [Support](https://trysilex.com/support/): Help with Silex: subscriptions and cancelling, restoring a purchase, the DNS shield, the Safari blocker, and how to reach a human.
